headline: OpenAI details Habitat’s multi-tenant storage and global latency design at 500 PB scale
summary: OpenAI’s Oct 23 engineering post describes the storage layer of Habitat, its online platform supporting products used by more than 1 billion people weekly. OpenAI reports returning to a co-managed multi-tenant Azure Cosmos DB design using an improved serverless mode with request-unit-based partition splits, and says it observed no provisioning or noisy-neighbor incidents for months after the change. It also reports that nearby replication, in-region caching and a Rust service reduced p50 read latency from roughly 120 ms to 10 ms. The article describes a change-data-capture system processing millions of changes per second. These are provider-reported production results; the post does not independently audit the telemetry or isolate each intervention’s contribution. Microsoft Learn’s public standard serverless documentation describes a different single-region, 5,000-RU/s-per-partition contract; OpenAI characterizes Habitat’s mode as an improved version built for it, and public availability is unclear.
